hook.line: Someone tells you Vale is leaving, or you see it with your own eyes: English says "I realised" or "I found out" for both. Spanish asks one question first: did it reach you from outside, or did it click inside your head?
hook.es: Me enteré de que Vale se va.
hook.en: I found out Vale is leaving.

examples.es: Me di cuenta de que había perdido las llaves.
examples.en: I realised I'd lost my keys.

examples.en: Hernando heard the news on the radio.

rule:
Use one test: where did the information come from?

*Darse cuenta de*: it clicks in your own head. You see, notice or work it out. *No me di cuenta de la hora.*

*Enterarse de*: it reaches you from outside. Someone tells you, or you read or hear it. *Me enteré de que Vale se va.*

Both are reflexive (*me*, *te*, *se*, *nos*) and both keep *de*: *de la hora*, *de que Vale se va*.

English "realise" often covers both, and "find out" too. In Spanish, ask yourself: did someone tell me, or did I notice? That decides it.

For news, gossip and "did you hear about…?", it is always *enterarse*.
smallPrint: Teachers call both of these reflexive phrases: the pronoun points back at you. You met each one on its own; this lesson sets them side by side.

readAndPick.es: Me di cuenta de que Simón no estaba.
options: Someone told me Simón wasn't there.
I noticed Simón wasn't there.
Simón noticed I wasn't there.

readAndPick.es: Me enteré de que Simón no estaba.
options: I noticed with my own eyes that Simón wasn't there.
Simón heard that I wasn't there.
I heard that Simón wasn't there.

readAndPick.es: ¿Te enteraste de que cierran el parque?
options: Did you hear they're closing the park?
Did you notice the park is closed?
Did I tell you they closed the park?

readAndPick.es: No me di cuenta de la hora.
options: Nobody told me the time.
I didn't notice the time.
I told you the time.

readAndPick.es: Hernando se enteró de la noticia por la radio.
options: Hernando noticed the radio was broken.
Hernando told the news on the radio.
Hernando heard the news on the radio.

readAndPick.es: Nos enteramos de que Altamira compró la cuadra.
options: We found out that Altamira bought the block.
We noticed that Altamira is buying the block.
They found out that we bought the block.

readAndPick.es: Vale se dio cuenta de que olvidó el azúcar.
options: Vale told us she forgot the sugar.
Vale realised she'd forgotten the sugar.
Someone told Vale about the sugar.
Did you hear about the mistake?
Did you tell me about the mistake?
Did you notice the mistake?

readAndPick.es: Me enteré de lo del incendio por Mariana.
options: I heard about the fire from Mariana.
I noticed the fire myself.
Mariana noticed the fire.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *me di cuenta* or *me enteré*, and type the whole sentence: *___ de que Vale se va.* (Someone told me Vale is leaving.)
yourTurn.answer: Me enteré de que Vale se va.
yourTurn.why: Someone told you, so the news came from outside: *enterarse*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *me di cuenta* or *me enteré*, and type the whole sentence: *___ de que había perdido las llaves.* (You worked out you'd lost your keys.)
yourTurn.answer: Me di cuenta de que había perdido las llaves.
yourTurn.why: It clicked in your own head: *darse cuenta*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I didn't notice the time. (I)
yourTurn.answer: No me di cuenta de la hora.
yourTurn.why: Noticing something yourself: *darse cuenta*, and *de* stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Did you hear about the fire?
yourTurn.why: "Did you hear about…?" is news arriving from outside: *enterarse*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Hernando heard the news on the radio. (past)
yourTurn.answer: Hernando se enteró de la noticia por la radio.
yourTurn.why: The news reached him from outside: *se enteró*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *we*: *Me enteré de que Vale se va.* (We found out Vale is leaving.)
yourTurn.answer: Nos enteramos de que Vale se va.
yourTurn.why: *Me* becomes *nos*, and the verb ending changes too.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Vale se dio cuenta del error.* (Vale didn't notice the mistake.)
yourTurn.answer: Vale no se dio cuenta del error.
yourTurn.why: *No* goes right before the pronoun and verb.

pitfalls.wrong: Me di cuenta de que Vale se va. (Someone told me.)
pitfalls.right: Me enteré de que Vale se va.
pitfalls.why: Almost. When the news comes to you from someone else, Spanish uses *enterarse*, not *darse cuenta*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me enteré de la hora. (I saw the clock.)
pitfalls.right: Me di cuenta de la hora.
pitfalls.why: When you notice something yourself, Spanish uses *darse cuenta*, not *enterarse*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me enteré que Vale se va.
pitfalls.right: Me enteré de que Vale se va.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The *de* stays before *que* with both of these phrases.

pitfalls.right: Me di cuenta de que perdí las llaves.
pitfalls.why: *Realizar* means to carry something out, not to realise it.

personal: Tell us one thing you noticed today with *me di cuenta de que…* and one thing you heard about recently with *me enteré de que…*.
